description: We are a team of Computer Science students interested in AI, satellite imagery and Earth observation. Our skills include software development, machine learning and data analysis. For the Be An Earth System Trend Detective challenge, we aim to explore satellite data to identify environmental changes and patterns over time and turn them into meaningful insights. We welcome collaboration with participants experienced in GIS, remote sensing, Earth science and data visualization.
summary:
GeoLens.ai is an interactive Earth observation intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It helps users investigate how Earth's systems change over time through three lenses: Water & Drought, Urban Heat & Growth, and Land Cover & Forest Change.

Users can explore geographic regions, compare areas, examine historical satellite observations, and analyze environmental trends through interactive maps, time-series visualizations, and statistical insights. The platform is designed around NASA Earth observation datasets, including MODIS Terra and Aqua, to help identify patterns such as declining vegetation, changing land cover, soil moisture variations, and increasing urban heat.

By transforming complex satellite observations into accessible visual evidence, GeoLens.ai aims to make Earth system trends easier to understand, investigate, and communicate, supporting more informed environmental research and decision-making.
details:
GeoLens.ai is an interactive Earth observation platform designed to help users investigate environmental changes through historical satellite data. Our current working prototype focuses on comparing vegetation greenness across six Karachi districts: Central, East, South, West, Korangi, and Malir.

Users can select two districts, define a historical time period, and compare their vegetation trends through interactive maps and time-series visualizations. The platform can scan district combinations to identify contrasting trends, rank comparisons by the estimated difference in their rates of change, and distinguish between increasing, decreasing, and uncertain vegetation trends. It also accounts for seasonal patterns, compares shared observation periods, and presents uncertainty estimates and sensitivity analysis to help users interpret results responsibly.

A key feature is the ability to compare NASA Terra and Aqua MODIS vegetation records using consistent observation periods and quality filters. Our implementation includes extraction pipelines for MODIS MOD13A3 v6.1 and MYD13A3 v6.1 through Google Earth Engine. The current demonstration uses simulated monthly NDVI observations, while real satellite-data extraction and validation are part of the next development milestone.

Technology and tools: We developed the frontend using React and TypeScript, with Three.js for the interactive Earth visualization and GSAP for interface animations. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, and NumPy for data processing, trend estimation, paired comparisons, uncertainty calculations, and sensitivity analysis. We also use Google Earth Engine for satellite-data extraction, OCHA administrative boundaries for geographic visualization, and Esri World Imagery for the satellite basemap.

Creative approach and impact: Rather than simply displaying satellite imagery, GeoLens transforms historical observations into comparable environmental evidence. Its district-pair scanning, cross-satellite comparison, seasonal adjustment, and uncertainty reporting help users identify areas that may deserve further investigation. Our intended impact is to support researchers, environmental organizations, and municipal teams in identifying vegetation changes and prioritizing potential field inspections. We emphasize transparent evidence and human-led decisions rather than treating satellite-derived trends as definitive explanations of environmental change.
